tools.name: closeCard
tools.description:
Close a virtual card.

and returned as `closed_reason`.

tools.name: createCard
tools.description:
Create a virtual card.

Issues one sandbox USD card to one of your customers. The card starts at `balance: 0` with
no spend limits, and every later call on this surface moves or gates that balance.

`customer.first_name`, `customer.last_name` and `customer.email` are required; the customer
is validated and then **not stored** — no name or email is persisted on the card, so a
leaked card id carries no PII with it. `reference` is yours, unique per business (a repeat
returns `409 duplicate_reference`), and defaults to the card id. `currency` may only be
`USD`; sending anything else returns 400.

The three limits are optional at issue time and are set or cleared later on
`POST /cards/{id}/spend_limits`. They are per-card ceilings you choose, and no platform maximum
is applied to any single axis. FirstFlip's ceilings sit elsewhere: one on how many cards a key
may hold open, and one on what all your cards may spend together — both stated below and in
the authorization section.

FirstFlip's one cap on issuing is a count, not an amount: a key may hold **250 open cards**.
The 251st `POST /cards` answers `409 card_limit_reached` with `param: cards` and nothing moves;
closing a card frees a slot, so a healthy integration is never locked out. Resending the same
`Idempotency-Key` is not a new card and is not counted.

The response shows `number_last4`, `expiry_month` and `expiry_year`. Those are minted here
for shape only — this card has no issuer, no full PAN and no CVV, and `sandbox.real_card`
says so on every answer. Requires an `Idempotency-Key` header.

Live mode: a live key is refused here before the body is read — issuing a real card needs the
cardholder rail FirstFlip has not built, so this answers `403 live_precondition_unmet` with
`param: cardholder`. No card is minted, and the refusal is what your key replays.


Requires scope `cards:write` on the business key. Test keys simulate supported operations; live execution depends on business eligibility and enabled service gates.

MCP requires an explicit idempotency_key. Reuse it with identical arguments to retry the same logical request.

body.description: JSON request body. Issue a card for one of your customers.

currency.description: Optional, and only ever `USD`. Anything else is `400 invalid_parameter` rather than a fallback.

reference.description: Your id for this card. Unique per key and mode; defaults to the generated `id`. A second attempt with the same reference and a different Idempotency-Key answers `409 duplicate_reference`.

customer.description:
Who the card is for. Only these three fields are accepted, and nothing about the customer is stored —
the same rule virtual accounts hold. Names and emails live in your database; the card carries your
`reference` so you can join them back.

email.description: Must be a valid address: `someone@app` is rejected, `someone@app.co` is not.

daily_limit.description: Rolling-24h authorization ceiling in major units. Omit or null for no ceiling.

per_transaction_limit.description: Largest single authorization in major units. Omit or null for no ceiling.

monthly_limit.description: Rolling-30-day authorization ceiling in major units. Omit or null for no ceiling.

tools.name: freezeCard
tools.description:
Freeze a virtual card.

Stops the card from spending or being withdrawn from, and keeps every other property — the
balance, the limits, the id — exactly as they are. `reason` (max 200 chars) is stored and
returned as `frozen_reason`.

Freezing is idempotent by outcome: freezing an already-frozen card answers `200` with that
state rather than an error, so two racing requests cannot disagree. A closed card answers
`409 card_closed`. Requires an `Idempotency-Key` header.

Live mode: this leg runs live, and it is the leg that matters on the day a card is reported lost.


Requires scope `cards:write` on the business key. Test keys simulate supported operations; live execution depends on business eligibility and enabled service gates.

MCP requires an explicit idempotency_key. Reuse it with identical arguments to retry the same logical request.

tools.name: fundCard
tools.description:
Fund a virtual card.

Puts money on the card from your business's sandbox funding, and returns the ledger row that
describes the credit (`type: topup`, `status: completed`, with `balance_before` and
`balance_after`). The row and the balance move in one commit, so a funding row can never
describe money the card did not receive.

Funding a **frozen** card is allowed — money arriving is never blocked by a freeze, only money
leaving. Funding a **closed** card returns `409 card_closed`. Requires an `Idempotency-Key`
header: retry the same key to replay this credit instead of funding twice.

Live mode: refused — funding needs a tenant USD balance to move money from, and that rail is not
built. This answers `403 live_precondition_unmet` with `param: funding` before your amount is read.


Requires scope `cards:write` on the business key. Test keys simulate supported operations; live execution depends on business eligibility and enabled service gates.

MCP requires an explicit idempotency_key. Reuse it with identical arguments to retry the same logical request.

amount.description:
Major units with at most two decimals (so `10.005` is a `400`, and so are `true`, `[]` and `"10"` —
no coercion, because a silently converted amount is a reconciliation break you find later).

is exactly that UTC day, and consecutive windows never count an object twice.

List a card's transactions.

The card's own ledger, newest first: every credit, withdrawal and authorization attempt,
approved or declined. This is the reconciliation source — the rows sum to the card's
`balance`, and a declined row carries the `decline_code` that explains it.

Filter by `type` (`topup`, `withdrawal`, `authorization`) and/or `status` (`completed`,
`approved`, `declined`), by a `created_from`/`created_before` window, and page with `limit`
plus `starting_after`.

Live mode: refused — the rows behind a live card are the issuer's, and they are not synced into this
platform yet. An empty list would read as "this card has spent nothing", which is a guess, so this
answers `403 live_precondition_unmet` with `param: transaction_sync`.


Requires scope `cards:read` on the business key. Test keys simulate supported operations; live execution depends on business eligibility and enabled service gates.

tools.name: simulateCardAuthorization
tools.description:
Simulate a card authorization.

The stand-in for a live purchase, and the only way to see an approval or a decline on this
surface. An **approved** authorization is the debit: the ledger row (`type: authorization`,
`status: approved`) and the balance drop commit together. A **declined** one writes the row
with `status: declined` and a `decline_code`, and moves no money.

The decline reason is decided in this order: `card_frozen`, `over_per_transaction_limit`,
`over_daily_limit`, `over_monthly_limit`, `over_tenant_monthly_limit`, `insufficient_funds`.
Code your retry logic against those six — a frozen card and an over-limit card are different
customer conversations, and `insufficient_funds` is the one a top-up fixes.
`over_tenant_monthly_limit` is the only one of the six that is not yours to set: it is a
ceiling FirstFlip places on what all of your cards may spend in a rolling 30 days
(**$1,000,000** of approved authorization spend per business).

Every answer is `201`: a decline is a recorded outcome of a real request, not a failed one.
A closed card is the exception and answers `409 card_closed`. Requires an `Idempotency-Key`
header — the same key cannot approve and decline two different attempts.

Live mode: refused with `403 live_mode_unavailable`, and this is the one leg that will stay that way.


Requires scope `cards:write` on the business key. Test keys simulate supported operations; live execution depends on business eligibility and enabled service gates.

MCP requires an explicit idempotency_key. Reuse it with identical arguments to retry the same logical request.

amount.description: The swipe, in major units with at most two decimals.

merchant.description:
Free text, stored on the row. It does not change the verdict: no merchant category, country or channel
is evaluated, because nothing here settles. Send it anyway — it is the field your reconciliation will
want when this lane goes live.

idempotency_key.description: Required by MCP writes. One stable key per logical operation; reuse it with identical arguments after a timeout. The CLI generates and prints a key when omitted.

tools.name: unfreezeCard
tools.description:
Unfreeze a virtual card.

Returns a frozen card to `active` and clears `frozen_reason`. A frozen card keeps its balance,
so unfreezing restores spending without funding it again.

A closed card cannot be reopened — `409 card_closed` says to issue a new one. Unfreezing a card
that is already active answers `200` with its current state. Requires an `Idempotency-Key`
header. No request body is read.

Live mode: this leg runs live with the same ordering as freeze — the issuer releases the card first,
and our record follows only if it agrees. A refusing issuer answers `503 service_unavailable` and the
card stays `frozen`.


Requires scope `cards:write` on the business key. Test keys simulate supported operations; live execution depends on business eligibility and enabled service gates.

MCP requires an explicit idempotency_key. Reuse it with identical arguments to retry the same logical request.

tools.name: updateCardSpendLimits
tools.description:
Update a card's spend limits.

Sets the merchant-side ceilings an authorization is judged against. Send at least one of
`daily_limit`, `per_transaction_limit` or `monthly_limit`; the axes you leave out are left
alone, and an explicit `null` clears that axis (no ceiling).

`daily_limit` and `monthly_limit` are rolling windows — 24 hours and 30 days from now, not a
calendar day or month — and they are summed from the **committed** approvals at the moment the
spend lands, not from a read taken earlier. That is what makes the ceiling hold when thirty
authorizations arrive at once. `per_transaction_limit` is a single-authorization maximum and is
checked before either window. Requires an `Idempotency-Key` header.

Live mode: refused — the issuer has rejected every amount format this platform has tried on that
call, and a ceiling sent in the wrong unit is worse than none. Writing it only on our side would be
a limit a live card does not actually obey, so this answers `403 live_precondition_unmet` with
`param: limit_format`.


Requires scope `cards:write` on the business key. Test keys simulate supported operations; live execution depends on business eligibility and enabled service gates.

MCP requires an explicit idempotency_key. Reuse it with identical arguments to retry the same logical request.

id.description: The card id (`card_test_…`) returned when the card was issued.

body.description:
JSON request body. Change the spend ceilings. Only the axes you name are written: an omitted field means "leave it alone",
an explicit `null` means "remove that ceiling". That distinction is the whole point — a partial update
cannot silently unlimit an axis you forgot to send.

idempotency_key.description: Required by MCP writes. One stable key per logical operation; reuse it with identical arguments after a timeout. The CLI generates and prints a key when omitted.

tools.name: withdrawCard
tools.description:
Withdraw from a virtual card.

Takes money back off the card (`type: withdrawal`, `status: completed`). The same commit rule
as funding applies: row and balance move together.

A withdrawal is refused with `409 card_not_active` unless the card is `active` — a freeze stops
money leaving, and a close stops everything (`409 card_closed`). An amount larger than the
balance returns `400 insufficient_balance` with `param: amount`, and nothing moves. Requires
an `Idempotency-Key` header.

Live mode: refused — taking real money off a card needs the withdrawal rail, and FirstFlip has not
proved that provider verb yet. This answers `403 live_precondition_unmet` with `param: withdrawal`
before your amount is read.
